Gold.note: Central bank accumulation and geopolitical safe-haven demand support elevated momentum.

Silver.note: Robust photovoltaic industrial demand and structural inventory deficits drive outperformance.

Copper.note: Tight concentrate markets and grid electrification demand outpace constrained mine supply.

Uranium.note: Structural primary supply deficit and global nuclear restarts support long-term contract pricing.

Lithium.note: Near-term oversupply from new global projects coincides with a normalization in EV growth rates.

Nickel.note: Surging Indonesian supply growth outpaces sluggish stainless steel and battery sector demand.

Zinc.note: Low treatment charges and European smelter curtailments tighten refined metal availability.

Iron Ore.note: Persistent weakness in Chinese real estate starts caps steel demand despite infrastructure stimulus.

Coal.note: Ample global thermal coal inventories and European demand destruction offset seaborne tightness.

Rare Earths.note: Opaque pricing and export controls balance against steady EV motor and wind turbine demand.

Manganese.note: South African rail and port logistics bottlenecks tighten seaborne supply for global steelmakers.

PGM.note: Declining internal combustion engine sales weigh on auto-catalyst demand despite hydrogen upside.

Potash.note: Steady global agricultural application rates balance with normalized supply from Eastern Europe.

Aluminum.note: Chinese capacity caps and rising green-energy demand tighten primary metal market balances.

Diversified.note: Balanced exposure to resilient precious metals and tight base metals offsets iron ore weakness.
